summary: Approved the final local Node.js 24/React/TypeScript/Vite dashboard architecture with an unchanged OpenAPI contract, fixed same-origin development proxy, deterministic-first evidence UI, safe accessible rendering, and reproducible unit/browser verification.
decisions: ADR-0005 enables the previously disabled frontend as the final bounded local-prototype component using Node.js 24 LTS, React, strict TypeScript, Vite, and npm with a committed package-lock.json. Database, authentication, persistence, analytics, provider access from the browser, and deployment remain disabled.

The dashboard is one in-memory page. Its page shell, analysis controller, generated-contract adapter, source/fact views, five-rule results, Gemini status/findings view, evidence explorer, and shared accessible primitives have explicit boundaries; child display components do not fetch and no router/global store/service worker is required.

The browser invokes only bodyless POST /api/v1/analyze-demo at the relative same-origin path. Vite binds locally and proxies only /api to the exact source-controlled allowlisted target http://127.0.0.1:8000. No API-origin/provider VITE variable, user/query-selected target, backend CORS change, or deployed reverse proxy is introduced.

contracts/openapi.yaml is sufficient and unchanged, so contract_change=false. The frontend generates and commits frontend/src/api/generated/schema.d.ts from OpenAPI and supplies deterministic generate:api/check:api scripts; freshness verification fails if regeneration changes the committed output.

Network input begins as unknown and passes bounded HTTP/content/top-level/discriminant guards before generated types are adapted. Generated TypeScript types provide compile-time alignment but do not make browser input trusted or create a competing runtime contract.

The analysis state is exactly idle, loading, success, pipeline_error, or client_error. One AbortController and duplicate-submit protection prevent concurrent/stale updates; user retry begins a fresh analysis and never merges evidence from different responses.

Every HTTP 200 renders deterministic content first. Gemini success adds explicitly non-authoritative candidate text; configuration_error, timeout, provider_error, invalid_output, and invalid_evidence retain all deterministic results. Typed HTTP 500 shows only its public pipeline code/message with no fabricated partial result; network/incompatible responses show a generic bounded client error.

All five rule results remain visible, including completed zero-signal states. Source metadata, observed facts, deterministic signals, Gemini candidates, missing evidence, limitations, and sanitized metadata remain visually and semantically distinct; no state is labeled as fraud, healthcare risk, payment/coverage/coding/clinical correctness, or a clean bill.

Evidence navigation resolves exact references only within the current response evidence_index. Safe application-generated DOM target indexes avoid using returned evidence strings as selectors/URLs/HTML; activation moves focus to evidence, a return control restores invoking focus, and missing/duplicate targets produce visible inert data-integrity warnings.

Every API/FHIR/model string is untrusted plain text rendered through React interpolation. dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, HTML/Markdown execution, untrusted URLs/selectors/styles/scripts, raw-body/exception display, browser secrets/config, persistent storage, export/download, and mutation actions are prohibited.

Accessibility requires native semantics, header/main/footer landmarks, skip navigation, logical headings/order, keyboard operation, visible focus, restrained live status, WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, non-color status cues, responsive narrow/desktop layouts, reduced-motion behavior, and deliberate focus movement/return for evidence.

Vitest and Testing Library cover adapters, states, interaction, focus, and inert rendering. Playwright Chromium covers assembled success/fallback/error flows, keyboard/evidence behavior, an automated accessibility scan, representative responsive widths, reduced motion, and one real Vite-to-FastAPI proxy smoke with Vertex AI explicitly disabled.

Infrastructure impact is true only because CI must explicitly provision Node.js 24, run npm ci, install the lock-matched Playwright Chromium runtime, and make frontend checks available to agentctl verification. No application hosting, cloud resource, container, domain, TLS, CDN, or deployment infrastructure is selected.

Required frontend evidence is npm ci; check:api; lint; typecheck; unit tests; production build; Playwright tests; and npm audit at high severity. Required checks fail rather than skip when Node, Chromium, audit service, or tooling is unavailable, while existing backend/OpenAPI/agentic/Python audit/security/source-integrity checks continue.

The user-approved architecture is bounded to the final local prototype. Any new API behavior, arbitrary input/target, persistent/browser provider state, authentication, shared deployment, real PHI, or consequential healthcare action requires a new feature, contract/architecture reconciliation, and security review.

risks.description: FHIR-derived or Gemini text could be executed or used in unsafe browser contexts, causing injection, misleading navigation, or disclosure.
risks.mitigation: Render returned values only as React text, prohibit HTML/Markdown/URL/style/script evaluation, generate safe DOM indexes, keep navigation response-local, and test adversarial HTML/instruction-like strings as inert text.

risks.description: The dashboard could visually elevate candidate model output or zero-signal rule results into authoritative fraud, payment, coverage, coding, clinical, or correctness conclusions.
risks.mitigation: Render deterministic content first, keep every information class separate, label Gemini as candidate/non-authoritative, preserve limitations/human authority, and prohibit decision/risk-score styling or language.

risks.description: A generalized dev proxy or configurable browser API origin could expand network access, leak configuration, or prompt an unapproved backend/CORS/deployment change.
risks.mitigation: Use only the relative operation and an exact source-controlled /api proxy target at 127.0.0.1:8000; prohibit API/provider browser environment variables and test the fixed path/target.

risks.description: Compile-time OpenAPI types or malformed evidence relationships could be treated as runtime proof, leading to crashes, stale data, or incorrect evidence focus.
risks.mitigation: Guard unknown transport/discriminants, use one replace-on-retry state, abort stale requests, build an exact response-local evidence map, and visibly degrade missing/duplicate targets.

risks.description: Node/npm and Playwright add supply-chain, reproducibility, audit-availability, browser-download, and CI-version drift risk.
risks.mitigation: Pin Node major 24, commit package-lock.json/generated types, use npm ci, install lock-matched Chromium explicitly, require clean generation/build/tests and fail-closed high-severity npm audit.

risks.description: A polished local unauthenticated dashboard could be mistaken for an approved production/shared deployment or real-healthcare workflow.
risks.mitigation: Keep local/synthetic/human-authority notices in the page and documentation, bind locally, select no deployment target, and require new identity/security/architecture work before any shared or real-data use.

risks.description: Visual polish could mask keyboard, focus, live-region, contrast, responsive, or reduced-motion failures.
risks.mitigation: Make accessibility behavior contractual and cover role/name queries, keyboard/focus return, automated browser scanning, desktop/mobile viewports, contrast review, and reduced-motion emulation.

notes_for_next_agent: Orchestrator: before lifecycle advancement requires operational consistency, enable frontend in .ai/project.json with the approved technology, add required frontend verification/security commands, provision Node.js 24 and Playwright Chromium in CI, and correct only the stale non-interface placeholder sentence in contracts/README.md. Do not change OpenAPI semantics.

Orchestrator: contract_change=false; validate the unchanged contracts/openapi.yaml and do not start database or backend workers. Infrastructure/tooling reconciliation is orchestrator-owned; frontend and independent testing are required.

Gemini frontend owner: read AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, the feature, this report, SYSTEM.md, ADR-0005, FRONTEND.md, and OpenAPI. Work only in the permitted frontend/tests/README/report paths and call only the relative bodyless operation.

Gemini frontend owner: implement the explicit controller/component/evidence boundaries, generated types, fixed proxy, safe text rendering, accessible focus/navigation, all states, npm scripts, contract-shaped fixtures, Playwright coverage, and local setup; never edit backend, contracts, task.json, project architecture, or workflows.

Gemini frontend owner: record npm ci, check:api, lint, typecheck, unit, build, e2e, and audit evidence in frontend-report.json, then run scope check FRONTEND-001 frontend. Browser tests must fake responses or explicitly disable Vertex AI and must not need credentials.

Tester: independently cover every model status and pipeline code, transport incompatibility/network retry, abort/no-concurrent-submit, inert adversarial text, exact evidence focus/return and unresolved targets, semantic/a11y/responsive/reduced-motion behavior, generated-type freshness, fixed proxy smoke, npm lock/audit, and no credential/config/browser persistence.

Security/reviewer: verify the exact integrated commit preserves the unchanged API/backend one-call boundary, fixed local target, plaintext-only rendering, deterministic/model authority separation, local/synthetic wording, accessibility, dependency evidence, and absence of database/auth/deployment expansion.
The human manually starts Gemini only after agentctl advances FRONTEND-001 to IMPLEMENTATION and the orchestrator prepares the frontend worktree; Codex must not claim to have started Gemini.
